questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All P are G.

Il. Some B are G.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some B are not P.

II. All G are P.

III. Some G are P.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
**Given **Statements:

I. All P are G.

Il. Some B are G.

The least possible Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e49bdd1c0018fe1d6f819188a4b5ec1e0c63d172a60f80480348282307707dee.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some B are not P. - **False **(Because, there is no relation between B and P, so it can be possible only)

II. All G are P. - **False **(Because, All P are G, so some G can be P but all G can never be P)

III. Some G are P. - **True **(Because, All P are G, so some G are P)

So, Only conclusion III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusion III follows".**

⇒ 4 × 6 × 7 - 8 ⇒ 168 - 8 = 160

Similarly,

⇒ 8 × 5 × 6 - 10 ⇒ 240 - 10 = **230**

questions.question: The government of India to introduced a new economic policy in ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1991**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The government of India introduced a new economic policy in 1991, which marked a significant shift in India's economic structure.
 
• The policy is known for initiating economic liberalization, privatization, and globalization, often abbreviated as LPG.
 
• The reforms were aimed at opening up the Indian economy to the global market and reducing the control of the government on various economic activities.
 
• The 1991 economic policy was a response to a severe balance of payments crisis that India was facing at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Liberalization**

 
 
• Economic liberalization refers to the process of reducing government regulations and restrictions in an economy to encourage greater participation of private entities.
 
• In the context of India, it involved reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and reducing taxes to attract foreign investment.
 
 
 
• **Privatization**
 
 
• Privatization is the transfer of ownership, property, or business from the government to the private sector.
 
• In India, this process involved the sale of state-owned enterprises to private entities to increase efficiency and profitability.
 
 
 
• **Globalization**
 
 
• Globalization is the process of interaction and integration among people, companies, and governments worldwide.
 
• In 1991, India embraced globalization by allowing foreign companies to operate in the Indian market and encouraging Indian companies to expand their operations globally.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments Crisis**
 
 
• The balance of payments crisis in India in 1991 was a situation where the country faced a severe shortage of foreign exchange reserves.
 
• To address this, India had to pledge its gold reserves to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and undertake significant economic reforms.

questions.question: What is the sex ratio in India as per the 2011 census (Females per Thousand Males)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**943**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The sex ratio in India as per the 2011 census is **943 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This figure represents an improvement from the 2001 census, where the sex ratio was 933 females per 1000 males.
 
• The sex ratio is an important indicator of gender balance in a population, reflecting the social and economic status of women in society.
 
• The 2011 census data was collected and compiled by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio:**

 
 
• The sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in a given population.
 
• It is a significant demographic indicator that helps in understanding the gender composition of a society.
 
• A balanced sex ratio is indicative of a healthy and equitable society where both genders have equal opportunities for survival and development.
 
• Historically, many regions have shown a skewed sex ratio due to cultural, social, and economic preferences for male children.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census:**
 
 
• The 2011 Census of India was the 15th National Census conducted since 1871.
 
• It was carried out in two phases: House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010) and Population Enumeration (9th to 28th February 2011).
 
• The census provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters including population size, sex ratio, literacy rate, and more.
 
• It serves as a critical tool for planning, policy formulation, and administration by the government.
 
 
 
• **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India:**
 
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India is responsible for conducting the decennial Census of India.
 
• This position is under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The organization collects, compiles, and publishes demographic data that is essential for national planning and development.

questions.question: Which dance form from West Bengal combines elements of classical dance with martial arts, and its movements often depict stories from Indian mythology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional Indian dance form that combines elements of classical dance with martial arts.
 
• It is particularly popular in the states of **West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand**.
 
• The movements in Chhau often depict stories from Indian mythology, including the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas.
 
• **Masks** are a significant aspect of the dance, especially in the Purulia Chhau from West Bengal, where dancers wear elaborate and colorful masks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the eight major Indian classical dances.
 
• It originated in a village named Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form is known for its impressive footwork and expressive eye movements.
 
• It typically narrates stories from Hindu epics and Puranas.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by intricate body movements and expressive gestures.
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms in India, with roots tracing back to ancient temples.
 
• The dance often depicts religious themes and spiritual ideas.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam**
 
 
• Mohiniattam is a classical dance form from Kerala.
 
• It is known for its graceful movements and feminine style.
 
• The term "Mohiniattam" comes from "Mohini" (a mythical enchantress) and "attam" (graceful body movements).
 
• This dance form primarily focuses on themes of love and devotion.
 
 
 
• **Chhau**
 
 
• Chhau is performed during festivals and special occasions.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).
 
• Purulia Chhau uses masks, while the other two styles do not.
 
• The dance involves vigorous and energetic movements, often resembling martial arts.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the first woman Chairperson of the Railway Board?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaya Varma Sinha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jaya Varma Sinha has become the **first woman to be appointed as the Chairperson of the Railway Board**, the apex body of the Indian Railways.
 
• Her appointment marks a significant milestone in the history of Indian Railways, reflecting the growing role of women in leadership positions within the organization.
 
• Before being appointed as the Chairperson, **she has held various key positions within the Indian Railways**, showcasing her extensive experience and expertise in the field.
 
• Jaya Varma Sinha is known for her **dedication and contributions to the development and modernization of the Indian Railways**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Railway Board**

 
 
• The Railway Board is the apex body of the Indian Railways and functions under the Ministry of Railways, Government of India.
 
• It is responsible for the overall administration, management, and policy formulation for the Indian Railways.
 
• The Railway Board consists of a Chairman, a Financial Commissioner, and other functional members who oversee various aspects such as engineering, traffic, mechanical, and staff services.
 
• The Board plays a crucial role in the planning and execution of railway projects, ensuring the efficient functioning of the vast railway network in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways**
 
 
• Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world, operating under the Ministry of Railways, Government of India.
 
• It plays a vital role in the transportation of passengers and goods across the country, connecting remote areas and facilitating economic growth.
 
• Indian Railways has a vast network of tracks, trains, stations, and employees, making it a critical component of India's infrastructure.
 
• The organization is constantly working on modernization and expansion projects to improve efficiency, safety, and passenger experience.
 
 
 
• **Women in Leadership**
 
 
• The appointment of women in leadership roles is a significant step towards gender equality and empowerment.
 
• It reflects the growing recognition of women's capabilities and contributions in various fields, including traditionally male-dominated sectors like railways.
 
• Encouraging women to take up leadership positions helps in fostering diversity and bringing diverse perspectives to decision-making processes.
 
• Organizations benefit from inclusive leadership, which can lead to better problem-solving, innovation, and overall performance.

questions.question: In India, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed ___________ of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State in India shall not exceed **one-third** of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
 
• However, the total number of members in the Legislative Council should not be less than 40.
 
• The provision for the Legislative Council is given in Article 171 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Not all states in India have a Legislative Council; it exists only in a few states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Council**

 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Parishad, it is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• Members of the Legislative Council are either elected by the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, or are nominated by the Governor.
 
• The tenure of a member of the Legislative Council is 6 years, with one-third of the members retiring every 2 years.
 
• The presence of a Legislative Council helps in providing a revising chamber to the Legislative Assembly and acts as a check on hasty legislation.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly**
 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Sabha, it is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly are directly elected by the people of the state through general elections.
 
• The tenure of the Legislative Assembly is 5 years unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The Legislative Assembly is responsible for making laws on the state list and concurrent list subjects, as well as controlling the state's finances.

questions.question: __________ represents a potential for further intellectual growth and contribution to economic-socio-cultural development of society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Literacy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Literacy enables individuals to acquire knowledge and develop critical thinking skills, which are essential for personal and societal growth.
 
• High literacy rates are often correlated with economic development and social progress, as literate populations are better equipped to participate in the economy and contribute to social and cultural advancements.
 
• Literacy is a fundamental human right and a cornerstone for achieving other rights, empowering individuals to improve their living standards and participate fully in community and national affairs.
 
• Promoting literacy can help reduce poverty and inequality by providing people with the skills needed to access better employment opportunities and improve their quality of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• It is conducted periodically by governments to collect data on the population's size, distribution, and various demographic characteristics.
 
• This data is crucial for planning and delivering public services, such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure.
 
• In many countries, censuses are conducted every ten years.
 
 
 
• **Economy**
 
 
• The economy refers to the system of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services within a society or geographic area.
 
• It encompasses various sectors, including agriculture, industry, and services, and is influenced by factors such as government policies, market conditions, and global trends.

questions.question: The portion of agricultural produce which is sold in the market by the farmers is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**marketed surplus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Marketed surplus** refers to the portion of agricultural produce that is sold in the market by farmers after meeting their own consumption and other non-commercial needs.
 
• This surplus is a critical indicator of the level of commercialization in agriculture, reflecting how much of the produce is available for trade and sale.
 
• The marketed surplus can vary widely depending on the type of crop, the level of agricultural productivity, and the economic conditions of the farmers.
 
• A higher marketed surplus generally indicates better economic conditions for farmers and a more vibrant agricultural market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Produce**

 
 
• Agricultural produce includes all the crops, fruits, vegetables, and other products that are cultivated or grown by farmers.
 
• These products can be for personal consumption, feeding livestock, or for selling in the market.
 
 
 
• **Produced Surplus**
 
 
• Produced surplus refers to the total agricultural output that exceeds the needs of the farmer's household and is available for sale or trade.
 
• It is a broader term that includes marketed surplus but also considers any surplus that may not be immediately sold in the market.
 
 
 
• **Marketed Deficit**
 
 
• Marketed deficit refers to a situation where the agricultural produce is insufficient to meet the market demand.
 
• This can lead to higher prices and potential food shortages.
 
 
 
• **Produced Deficit**
 
 
• Produced deficit occurs when the total agricultural production is less than what is needed for both consumption and market sale.
 
• This could be due to poor yield, adverse weather conditions, or other factors affecting agricultural productivity.

questions.question: The Dandi March, led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, was a significant protest against which British policy?

__
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the Salt March, was a non-violent protest against the British monopoly on salt and the heavy salt tax imposed on Indians.
 
• Beginning on **March 12, 1930**, Gandhi and his followers marched from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat, covering approximately 240 miles over 24 days. 
 
• Upon reaching Dandi on **April 6, 1930**, Gandhi symbolically made salt from seawater, defying British law and sparking a widespread civil disobedience movement across India.
 
• The protest against the salt tax highlighted the unjust and oppressive policies of British rule and became a turning point in the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indigo Cultivation
 
 
• Indigo cultivation was forced upon Indian farmers under British rule, especially in Bengal and Bihar, to meet the high demand for indigo dye in Europe.
 
• The exploitative system led to the Indigo Rebellion (1859–1860) and later influenced movements like the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917, where Gandhi supported farmers against the oppressive indigo cultivation practices enforced by British planters.
 
 
 
• Textile Trade Regulations
 
 
• The British imposed trade regulations and heavy duties on Indian textiles while promoting British-made textiles in India.
 
• This led to the decline of India’s traditional textile industry, particularly handloom and Khadi.
 
• In response, the Swadeshi Movement (1905) encouraged Indians to boycott British goods, especially textiles, and promoted the use of Indian-made products, including Khadi, to revive the local industry.
 
 
 
• Land Revenue
 
 
• The British introduced various exploitative land revenue systems like the Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari systems, which led to excessive taxation and poverty among Indian farmers.
 
• Resistance to these policies included the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and other regional revolts where farmers protested against unfair land taxes and evictions.
